transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I’m constantly worried about how I look as I’m getting older, and it’s making me avoid family events and work presentations. It has become so overwhelming lately that I felt I finally needed to talk to someone about it.
When you worry about how you look, is it mainly about a specific flaw in your appearance that others may not notice, or is it more a general fear of being judged or embarrassed by other people?

It is definitely about very specific flaws that I focus on. I constantly fixate on the lines on my face and the loose, saggy skin under my jaw and neck, which I try to hide with scarves and check constantly in the mirror. My husband and daughter try to reassure me that I look fine, but I still feel convinced that I look completely worn out and terrible.
Do you feel that these appearance concerns might be exaggerated or possibly not as noticeable to others, or are you completely convinced they are real and severe despite reassurance?

I am completely convinced that these flaws are real and highly noticeable to everyone who looks at me. Even though my husband and daughter constantly reassure me that I look fine, their words never feel reassuring enough. I still feel deeply ashamed of my sagging jawline and worn-out appearance, and I just can't shake the feeling that it's all people see.

Have you ever tried to get these appearance concerns checked by a doctor or cosmetic specialist, and if so, what did they tell you? Do you feel the worry is mainly about how you look, or more about being judged because of it?

I haven't seen any cosmetic specialists or other doctors for this, except for my primary care doctor who referred me to you. As for my worry, it is really a mix of both—I am highly fixated on the specific changes in my face and neck, but I also feel a deep shame and dread about other people seeing me and judging me.
Have you ever had any doubt that these appearance flaws might be less noticeable than they seem to you, or are you completely certain they are truly there and obvious to everyone?

I am completely certain that they are obvious to everyone, and I don't have any doubts. When I look in the mirror or under bright lights, the loose skin and wrinkles look so clear and terrible that I know others must see them the exact same way. My family tries to reassure me, but I truly feel they are just being nice to protect my feelings.

Have you ever believed that other people are specifically talking about, mocking, or targeting you because of these appearance concerns, or is your worry mainly about how you look and being judged for it?

No, I don't think people are actively targeting or mocking me. My worry is deeply centered on how worn out I look compared to the younger women at my firm, especially with the loose skin under my jaw, and I have an intense fear of being judged, seen in bright light, or photographed.
Have you ever believed that other people are secretly talking about you, mocking you, or trying to harm you because of your appearance, even when there is no clear evidence?

No, I don't believe anyone is trying to harm me or secretly mocking me behind my back. It is just that I feel incredibly self-conscious and ashamed of my aging appearance, and I constantly worry about how worn out I must look to others.

When you avoid family events or work presentations, is it mainly because you fear people will judge your appearance, or because you worry you will act awkwardly, blush, or say something embarrassing in front of others?

It is entirely because of how I look, not because I'm worried about acting awkwardly or saying the wrong thing. I just dread the thought of people seeing my saggy skin and wrinkles in bright light, or being captured in photographs at these events. I feel so ashamed of looking old and worn out that I would rather just avoid being seen at all.
Have you ever had similar concerns about other parts of your body or appearance, or is this problem limited to your face and neck?

No, my concerns are strictly limited to my face and neck, and I don't really worry about any other parts of my body. It is specifically the lines on my face and the loose skin under my jaw that make me feel so ashamed and want to hide from others.
When you avoid events or presentations, is your main fear that people will notice and judge your appearance, or that you might blush, tremble, or say something embarrassing in front of others?

My fear is entirely about how I look, specifically that people will notice how old, saggy, and worn out my face and neck look. I'm not worried about blushing, trembling, or saying the wrong thing at all. It is really just the shame of being seen in bright light or being photographed because of my appearance.

When you avoid family events or presentations, is the main reason that you fear people will notice a flaw in your appearance, or that you will be judged as awkward, inferior, or embarrassing even if your appearance were fine?

If I felt I looked fine, I wouldn't mind doing the presentations or going to family events at all. It is entirely because of the shame of being seen under bright lights or photographed looking so worn out and saggy. I just dread people noticing the loose skin under my jaw and the lines on my face.
If you felt your appearance was fine, would you still avoid family events or presentations because of fear of being judged, or would you feel comfortable going?

If I felt my appearance was fine, I would feel completely comfortable going and wouldn't avoid anything at all. In the past, I actually loved organizing our temple's cultural festivals and presenting my own design work to clients. My avoidance is entirely driven by the deep shame I feel over my wrinkles and loose skin, and the dread of being photographed or seen in bright light.

When you avoid events or presentations, is it mainly because you fear people will notice and judge a flaw in your appearance, or because you fear being embarrassed, awkward, or negatively judged even if your appearance were fine?

It is strictly because of my appearance. If I felt I looked fine, I wouldn't have any fear of being awkward or judged at all. The only thing stopping me is the dread of people noticing the loose skin under my jaw and how worn out I look.

Have you ever been completely convinced that other people can see these flaws exactly as you do, even when they tell you they cannot, or do you think there is a chance your concern may be more intense than what others notice?

Yes, I am completely convinced that these flaws are there and that others can see them just as clearly as I do. Even though my husband and daughter constantly reassure me and tell me I look fine, their words never feel true or reassuring to me. Deep down, I feel certain that I look worn out and saggy, and I am terrified of others seeing me in bright lighting, which is why I try so hard to hide my neck.

Do you ever feel anxious in social situations mainly because you might blush, tremble, or say something embarrassing, even when your appearance is not an issue? Or is the anxiety only about your specific appearance concerns?

My anxiety is strictly and entirely about my appearance, not about blushing, trembling, or saying something embarrassing. I only feel anxious because I dread people seeing my wrinkles and the saggy skin under my jaw, especially in bright light or photos. If I felt my appearance was fine, I wouldn't have any anxiety at all in these situations.
Have you ever had any moment of doubt that these appearance flaws might be less noticeable to others than they seem to you, or are you completely certain they are obvious and severe?

I'm not really sure, it just feels so obvious and real to me when I look in the mirror, but I haven't thought about it in terms of how certain I am. I just know that the loose skin and wrinkles are all I can see, and it makes me feel incredibly ashamed to be seen.
Do you believe these appearance flaws are definitely real and obvious to everyone, or do you think they might be exaggerated by your mind compared with how others see you?

My husband and daughter try to reassure me and say it's not that bad, but I am completely convinced that the loose skin and lines are highly visible to everyone. When I look in the mirror, it feels so real and undeniable to me. Because of that, it is really hard to believe anyone who tells me otherwise.
Do you believe these appearance flaws are definitely real and obvious to everyone, or do you think your mind may be making them seem worse than they really are?

To me, these flaws feel completely real and highly obvious, and I am convinced I look worn out and saggy, which is why I feel so ashamed to be seen. Even though my husband and daughter try to reassure me otherwise, their words don't help because when I look in the mirror, the loose skin and wrinkles are completely undeniable.

When you are with other people, is your main fear that they will notice and judge your appearance, or that you will be embarrassed, awkward, blush, tremble, or say the wrong thing even if your appearance were fine?

My fear is entirely about people noticing how saggy and worn out my face and neck look, not about blushing, trembling, or saying the wrong thing. If I felt my appearance was fine, I wouldn't have any of this anxiety or feel the need to avoid these situations at all. The distress I feel is completely focused on how I look.

Do you ever think there is a chance that your appearance concerns might be more severe in your mind than they appear to other people, or are you completely convinced that the flaws are truly as obvious and severe as they feel to you?

Even though my family tries to reassure me and says it's not that bad, I am completely convinced that the loose skin under my jaw and the lines on my face are extremely obvious and severe. I feel like they are just saying those things to be nice, but I truly believe I look as worn out and saggy as I feel.
Outside of these appearance concerns, do you also worry a lot about being judged, embarrassed, or acting awkwardly in social situations even when your looks are not an issue?

No, I don't think I worry about those things at all when my looks aren't an issue. My anxiety is almost always completely tied back to how I look and present myself to others. If I felt fine about my appearance, I would feel completely comfortable in social situations.
Outside of your appearance concerns, do you also worry a lot about being judged, embarrassed, or acting awkwardly in social situations even when your looks are not an issue?

No, not at all. My worries and avoidance are completely tied to how I look and my aging appearance. If my looks weren't an issue, I wouldn't have any fear of being judged or acting awkwardly in social situations.

When you are in social situations, is your main fear that people will notice and judge your appearance, or is it more that you might act awkwardly, blush, tremble, or say something embarrassing even if your appearance were fine?

My main fear is definitely about people noticing and judging my appearance, specifically looking old, worn out, or saggy in bright light or photos. If I felt my appearance was fine, I wouldn't worry at all about acting awkwardly or embarrassing myself, as I used to love organizing temple events and presenting my design work.

Do you worry this way only about your appearance, or do you also fear social situations because you might blush, tremble, say something embarrassing, or seem awkward even when your appearance is not an issue?

I only worry about my appearance and how old, saggy, and worn out my face and neck look. I don't have any fear of blushing, trembling, or saying the wrong thing. My anxiety is driven entirely by the dread of people seeing me in bright light or in photos.
Do you believe the loose skin and wrinkles are truly present and obvious to others, or do you think they may be more in your mind than in reality?

To me, the wrinkles and loose skin under my jaw feel completely real and glaringly obvious. Even though my family tries to reassure me otherwise, I am deeply convinced that I look worn out and saggy, and that others will immediately notice it, especially in bright lighting.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs about your appearance, such as thinking a body part is deformed, misshapen, or that something is wrong with your body that others say is not there?

No, I don't have any worries about other parts of my body being deformed or misshapen. My concerns are strictly focused on my face and the loose, saggy skin under my jaw that makes me look so worn out and terrible. My husband and daughter constantly reassure me that I look fine, but I just can't bring myself to believe them.

When you avoid social or work situations, is it only because you are worried about your appearance being noticed, or do you also fear being embarrassed, judged, or acting awkwardly even if your appearance were not a concern?

My avoidance is entirely because of my worries about my appearance. In the past, I never had any trouble presenting or socializing—in fact, I used to really enjoy those things. I only avoid them now because I feel so ashamed of looking saggy and old, but if my appearance weren't a concern, I wouldn't fear these situations at all.

When you avoid social or work situations, is it only because you worry people will notice your appearance, or do you also fear being embarrassed, judged, or acting awkwardly even if your appearance were not a concern?

It is completely because of my appearance. If my looks weren't a concern, I would gladly present my work and attend temple events like I used to enjoy doing. My only fear is that people will see how old and saggy my face and neck look.
Outside of your appearance concerns, do you also fear social situations because you might blush, tremble, say something embarrassing, or seem awkward even when your looks are not an issue?

No, I don't really experience those fears at all. My anxiety and avoidance in social situations are entirely related to how I look and my worries about my aging appearance, rather than fears of blushing, trembling, or saying something embarrassing.
Outside of your worries about your appearance, do you also fear social situations because you might be judged, embarrassed, or act awkwardly even when how you look is not an issue?

No, not at all. My fear and avoidance of social situations are almost entirely driven by my worries about my appearance and how I look. I don't have any general fear of acting awkwardly or being judged for other reasons when my appearance isn't an issue.
